recipes.name: How to Make Maryland Crab Cakes

steps.text: Preheat the oven’s broiler. Lightly grease a broiler pan or baking sheet with cooking spray.
Mix crabmeat, bread crumbs, parsley, salt, and pepper together in a large bowl.
Mix egg, mayonnaise, mustard, and hot sauce together in a small bowl; stir into crab mixture until well combined.
Form into patties and place on the prepared broiler pan or baking sheet.
Broil crab cakes under the preheated broiler until golden brown on both sides, about 5 to 7 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: How to Make Maryland Crab Cakes
raw_recipe.description: Maryland is famous for its crab cakes—try this delicious recipe made with crabmeat, bread crumbs, mustard, parsley and mayo and you’ll know why!

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make the ultimate Maryland crab cakes. Use the best crab meat you can afford. Gently combine the crab meat with just a little bit of bread crumbs, egg, mayonnaise and seasonings. Be sure not to overmix. The cakes are cooked directly under the broiler until lightly browned. Enjoy with a side salad, or on top of bread with a dollop of your favorite seafood sauce.

review.reviewBody: I'm from Maryland also. The recipe sounds OK except PLEASE don't shred the crab meat. It should stay in lumps and be handled gently. It's traditional to use Maryland's own Old Bay seasoning, not hot sauce. Also, when formed the cakes should be refrigerated for about half an hour, to firm up a little and prevent their breaking up in the pan.

This is the closest recipe to my Dad’s that I’ve found. I grew up crabbing off the Maryland shore and then steaming crabs on a wood fire outside with water, vinegar , salt and Old Bay in a huge kettle. We saved a few dozen to use lump back fin meat for our crabcakes. No hot sauce, but everything else was in them plus a bit more old bay. Dad did fry them in a cast iron skillet in a little butter til they had a nice brown tender crisp. A little lemon juice didn’t do any harm either.

My husband especially loved these. I basically followed the recipe with slight changes. Instead of hot sauce, I added 2 tsp of Old Bay Seasoning which contains salt and pepper which I omitted. I also added1/2 tsp lemon juice. I used 1/4 cup panko. Next time I will add a bit more mayonnaise to hold them together although I did follow another viewer’s suggestion and refrigerated them 30 minutes before broiling. I loved broiling them - less messy! They did need an extra minute or two per side but could be due to where i placed my oven racks. Thank you!

These were good, and I got around nine 2" crab cakes. I also added 1/2 tsp of Worcestershire sauce and 1 tsp of lemon juice (saw this on other recipes). I preferred to pan-fry these in some olive oil and butter. The first batch I did were falling apart, but the second batch really kept their shape (due to hotter pan?). I even refrigerated the mixture for an hour prior. Other recipes call for a lot more bread crumbs (1 1/2 cups for 1 lb crab), so I would increase the bread crumbs the next time (more, but not THAT much). I enjoyed these with Remoulade Sauce with Horseradish from this site. It gives these the kick they need.

Do not shred the crabmeat. Backfin is expensive, but far sweeter. Do not use imported, canned crab. Use one small egg as a binder. Substitute 8 - 10 saltine crackers for bread. Use a dash or two of "Wooster". If it is a Maryland (or better yet, Baltimore) crab cake, Old Bay Seasoning is de rigueur. Broil quickly; or pan fry in lard, using a seasoned cast iron skillet. Either way - do not overcook. You want to taste the crabmeat! Serve on a bed of lettuce. If a sandwich, use a thin brioche roll

Flavor was on point but it was a little dry.
I topped each cake with a pat of butter and a sprinkle of garlic. 
Next time I'll increase the wet ingredients slightly but I will be making them again!
Great base recipe, barely any filler, as I desired little to none! I added about 1 teaspoon lemon juice and 2 teaspoons old bay. Refrigerated mixture, and browned on my electric griddle.

I used Phillips refrigerated lump, lite mayo, reduced sodium Old Bay and some breadcrumbs. That's it. 8oz crab made 4 cakes using a 1/3 cup "mold". I baked it at 400 degrees on a greased baking sheet.

The overall recipe is great! I agree that Old Bay makes it Maryland. Also frying them after letting the cakes chill in the fridge for about 30 mins is perfect. If you don't let them chill, they will rebel and make things difficult. Nobody wants rebellious crab cakes, lol. Overall, the simplicity of not over adding to the crab is perfect! This comes from someone that grew up crabbing on the Chesapeake. Like lobster rolls, let the protein speak louder than the additives! Oh, for those complaining about canned crab, the recipe doesn't state that and not everyone has access to fresh crabs!
As suggested by others, I added Old Bay instead of hot sauce. I also allowed them to chill in the refrigerator for several hours before broiling them. They were absolutely delicious. We devoured them

Easy. Absolutely delicious! I used a very heavy dash old Old Bay for seasoning and we all loved them! I agree with other reviewers to NOT shred but leave it lumped! Part of the joy of eating a proper Maryland crabcake is getting the big lump to bite in to! These cooked up perfectly fine for me without refrigerating first ( as some reviewers have suggested. Certainly wouldn't be a bad idea, but I didn't have time and it didn't matter. They stayed bound together fine using an extra large egg.).

These came out very well! I took suggestions of adding Old Bay and a bit of Worcestershire. I let it sit a couple of hours in the fridge before broiling. They seemed a tad wet, but cooked up beautifully! Made an aioli for serving, will have to do this again. Much easier cleanup vs. frying.
Not Maryland style, without Old Bay, Worcestershire sauce and I must have Garlic in mine ( minced fresh)1 egg better, so not too liquidy.

I'm a Maryland boy, and always have leftover crab meat. I noticed several reviewers mentioned the absence of Old Bay. I steam my crabs in National Boe beer and copious amounts of Old Bay. If your crab meat has not been prepared with Old Bay, it's imperative that you add it to the mixture. Absolutely OUTSTANDING. After assembling the crab cakes, I was concerned they were too moist ,and wondered if I should squeeze them dry. A quick search on the internet said DO NOT SQUEEZE THEM DRY. I didn't and they were fantastic. They took the full 7 minutes on each side. I served them with a lemon slice and a simple aioli sauce on the side.

Aha! Never considered broiling but now i will!! Its healthier which is a current requirement ( bye bye butter frying ) in my kitchen. I really like this recipe but am cooking for someone who is on a salt restricted diet. There goes the old bay! However , i made this with lower sodium great value canned chicken breast.( i know) and called them chicken cakes ! Substituted cilantro for parsley, and used siracha . A hit for lunch with a salad . Easy and quick! Thanks!

I made this adding Old Bay and lemon wedges to our plates. They weren't very pretty although I used a 1/3 cup measurer because when I flipped them half way through, they broke apart. Nothing wrong with the taste though, and the lemon juice was great to bring out the lovely flavor of the sweet crab meat.
I added about 1 more T. of bread crumbs, 1/2 T. additional mayonnaise, a dash of garlic powder, and a good 2 dashes of Tabasco Sauce. The crab flavor came through very nicely--delicious!

A few comments. There is crab imperial... jumbo lump crabmeat with very little else added but just enough of these ingredients to hold it together for broiling. Maryland style crab cakes need some Old Bay seasoning and can be broiled or fried. I would never shred lump crabmeat! Those lumps are gold! Just my opinion as a girl from that area.
